note: Background references that informed Hearth's HCP brief tone and eval design. Our timelines and reports are synthetic team-authored data — we do not redistribute protected clinical corpora.

sources.title: Talking With Your Older Patients
sources.organization: National Institute on Aging (NIA), National Institutes of Health
how_we_use_it: Plain-language, respectful HCP-facing brief copy (no jargon dumps).
One-idea-at-a-time headlines and short change bullets for scanability in a short visit.
Encourage confirming understanding / contacting patient or caregiver rather than rushing to a label.
Face the person as a fellow adult — brief language stays non-patronizing.
key_takeaways_applied: Speak plainly; do not assume medical terminology is known.
Avoid hurrying; give time to process — our brief is one screen, not a chart dump.
Address the patient respectfully; involve caregivers when appropriate via contact_patient_or_caregiver.
Support teach-back style next steps (review evidence, then decide) instead of automated diagnosis.

related_nia_pages.title: Caring for Older Patients With Cognitive Impairment

sources.title: DementiaBank data access index
how_we_use_it: Methodological inspiration for longitudinal language / interaction signals (baseline vs later window).
Awareness that real dementia-language corpora exist (e.g. Pitt, Cookie Theft, fluency tasks) for future IRB-approved research.
Explicit non-use: this eval package does not download, mirror, or ship DementiaBank media or transcripts.
key_takeaways_applied: Separate control-like stable periods from changed periods when designing synthetic timelines.
Keep protocol vs naturalistic distinction in mind — Hearth uses consented family chat, not Cookie Theft tasks.
Access to DementiaBank requires contribution/agreement processes; cite the index, do not claim we trained on it.
sources.access_note: DementiaBank corpora are listed for researchers with signed contribution forms. Hearth eval cases (P01–P10) are fully synthetic and independent of those files.

disclaimer: Citing NIA and TalkBank does not imply endorsement by NIH, NIA, or TalkBank. Hearth briefs remain decision support only and are not a medical device or diagnostic tool.
